nodes.label: Bounded Browser Disconnect Grace
nodes.rationale: A 75 ms bounded delay lets child-process exit and close events arrive before the failure snapshot without materially extending the request.

nodes.label: Exact Browser Dependency Pinning
nodes.rationale: Exact pins prevent caret updates from silently separating the Puppeteer controller version from the deployed Chromium major version.

nodes.label: Disabled Unused Chromium Graphics
nodes.rationale: DOM text and Open Graph extraction do not need image or WebGL rendering, so disabling graphics removes an unused Chromium subsystem.

nodes.label: Reuse Chromium Launch Page
nodes.rationale: Reusing the initial Puppeteer page avoids creating an unnecessary second page and renderer process.

nodes.label: Literal Lazy Browser Imports
nodes.rationale: Literal dynamic imports expose Puppeteer and Sparticuz package roots to Next.js and Node File Trace while keeping browser loading lazy.

nodes.label: OOM Hypothesis Remains Unproven
nodes.rationale: Browser disconnect evidence does not distinguish OOM, Chromium crash, or external process termination; deployed memory and cgroup evidence is required.

nodes.label: Render-Wait Scroll Pressure Reduction
nodes.rationale: Repeated bottom scrolling could trigger unnecessary lazy Marketplace and recommendation rendering even though extraction only needs the existing primary-listing DOM.

nodes.label: Post-Deployment Vercel Verification
nodes.rationale: Static and local checks cannot establish success in the deployed Vercel Hobby browser runtime; one post-commit endpoint request remains required.

nodes.label: Zero-AI Deterministic Extraction
nodes.rationale: Listing URL and Facebook extraction remain deterministic and make no AI calls on the Free tier.

nodes.label: Node DNS Lookup Callback Shape Fix
Target-Evidence-First Login Classification
nodes.rationale: Ordinary Facebook login UI may be co-rendered with an anonymously readable Marketplace listing, so target listing evidence must be evaluated before login markers.

nodes.label: Literal Lazy Browser Imports
nodes.rationale: Literal dynamic imports expose Puppeteer and Sparticuz package edges to Next.js output tracing while retaining lazy server-only loading.

nodes.label: Browser and Chromium Process Lifecycle Diagnostics
Single-Page Serverless Browser Optimization
nodes.rationale: Reusing Chromium's initial page and avoiding repeated scrolling, duplicate viewport setup, and a synthetic user agent reduces browser work without removing Marketplace data.

nodes.label: Sparticuz ANGLE and SwiftShader Graphics Stack
nodes.rationale: Restoring Sparticuz's default graphics mode produces its supported ANGLE plus SwiftShader serverless path instead of retaining in-process GPU flags while disabling WebGL.
